lawyer:
MA Samad with MGH Ruhullah, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners 
Mahbubey Alam, Advocate ----- For the Respondent Contemners.
parties:
Solaiman (Md) and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Md Mosharaf Hossain Khan and others ----- Respondent Contemners
full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts are that the petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 3058 of 2001 before this court challenging the legality and propriety of preparation of the voter list for holding election of the executive committee of the Bangladesh Swimming Federation alleging that the preparation of voter list has not been properly done. They moved the aforesaid writ petition on 16-7-2001 when a Rule nisi was issued upon the respondents and pending hearing of the Rule the respondents were restrained from holding the election of the Bangladesh Swimming Federation hereinafter called "the federation" on 22-7-2001. It is alleged that the contemner respondents were verbally informed by the petitioners about the said order on 16th of July, 2001 and in writing they were informed on 18th July, 2001 but in spite of that the contemner opposite parties finally published the result of the election of the federation by taking advantage of the stay order obtained by them from the Appellate Division. 

 3. Here it may be mentioned that the contemner respondents after they came to know about the order dated 16th of July, 2001 passed by this court, filed an application for vacating the injunction order dated 16th of July, 2001 but that application was rejected by this court whereupon they filed a civil Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 464 of 2001 before the Appellate Division wherein they obtained the order of stay against which the present petitioners filed an application for vacating the order of stay before the Appellate Division and the Appellate Division after hearing the parties vacated the order of stay and directed the parties to get the writ petition heard as early as possible preferably by 31st by July. 2001. It is further alleged that during the period of stay granted by the Appellate Division in Chamber, the present contemners published the final result of the federation on 6-8-2001. It is further alleged that 17-7-2001 was fixed for scrutiny of the nomination paper and after scrutiny it was found that there was only one set of candidates and, as such, the preliminary result was declared on that date and thereafter the final publication was made as stated aforesaid. 

 9-6-2001 was fixed for publishing the draft of the voter list 10-7-2001 was fixed for the filling objection against the voter list, if any, 11-7-2001 was fixed for distribution of nomination papers and 15-7-2001 fixed for submission of nomination paper and 16-7-2001 was fixed for scrutiny and 17-7-2001 was fixed for withdrawal and election was to be held. Since there was only one panel for the posts the primary result was declared on 17th of July, 2001 but they did not publish the final result because of the pendency of the aforesaid writ petition and after obtaining stay from the Appellate Division in chamber on 30-7-2001 the contemner respondents published the final result on 6-8-2001 and the first meeting of the executive committee was held on 9-8-2001. The allegation of the petitioner is that after receipt of the Rule and the injunction order the contemner respondents by willfully disregarding and violating the court's order dated 16th of July, 2001 published the final result on 6-8-2001 by taking advantage of the stay order passed by the Appellate Division in chamber and thereby the contemner respondents not only disregarded and disobeyed the court's order but also rendered the aforesaid writ petition infructuous. 

 5. Mr MA Samad, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that even if it is conceded for argument's sake that the contemner opposite parties did not know of the court's order dated 16th of July, 2001 on 16-7-2001 but the admitted position is that they came to know about the aforesaid order on 18th of July, 2001 and thereafter initially they unsuccessfully moved this court against the order of injunction and then moved the Appellate Division and obtained the stay order on 30th of July, 2001 in chamber which was ultimately extended from time to time and taking advantage of that stay order, the final result of election was published on 6-8-2001 which clearly tantamount to contempt of court. The learned Advocate further submits that they have also published some misleading news items in different newspapers whereby also they have misinterpreted the facts and thereby committed act of contempt upon this court and the Appellate Division. The learned Advocate, referring to the different provisions of the constitution of the federation, submits that the Election Commissioners, namely, the present contemner respondent Nos. 2 and 3, were entrusted with the duty of holding the election of the Federation in their official capacity and since they are in the service of the Republic the instant application is maintainable. The learned Advocate further submits that even if it is admitted for argument's sake that the Federation is not a statutory body but it is controlled by the Bangladesh Swimming Council, a statutory body which provides for election of the federation under the supervision and control of the persons in the service of the Republic and therefore, this application is maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution. Mr MA Samad further submits that in their affidavit-in-opposition the contemner respondents- although pleaded for apology but they have also attempted to justify their action and, as such, the apology is not an apology in the eye of law and must be rejected. 

 6. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel appearing for the contemner respondent, raised a preliminary objection as to the maintainability of the writ petition itself in view of the fact that the Bangladesh Swimming Federation is not a statutory organisation therefore, any order passed by the election commissioner in the matter of holding election of the Federation cannot be called in question before this court under Article 102 of the Constitution inasmuch as it is now well settled that the federation is not a statutory body for which he relies on the case reported in 1992 BLD 596 = 45 DLR 360 [Shahabuddin vs Bangladesh]. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case the order passed by this court while issuing the Rule was for not holding the election on 22nd of July, 2001 but since there was only one set of candidates the preliminary result was published on 17th of July, 2001 after scrutiny of the nomination papers on 16th of July, 2001 and the preliminary result was finally published on 6th of August, 2001 by the contemner respondent Nos. 2 and 3. Therefore, in view of the admitted position they have not committed any contempt of this court inasmuch as no election of the federation was held on 22nd of July, 2001. The learned Counsel further submits that there are divergence of opinion as to the point of time when the stay order comes into force and he has referred to the following decisions namely, 47 CWN 186, 1960 PLR. West Pakistan) Vol 11 page 751, AIR 1992 (SC) 1439 and 1992 BLD 60 [Md Abdul Quddus vs Md Mustafa Hossain] Mr Alam submits that in 47 CWN 186. Calcutta High Court observed that a stay order made by the Appellate Court operates from the time it is passed. In the case reported in 1960 PLR (WP) 751 the Full Bench of West Pakistan following a Full Bench judgment of Lahore High Court [DLR 1955 (WPC) 3] held that a stay order comes into operation the moment the order is passed and it does not depend on anything other than the making the order. They further observed that the legal proposition does not admit of any doubt that an order passed by an inferior court during the subsistence of stay order made by a superior court is an absolute nullity. But in 1992 BLD 60 [Md Abdul Quddus vs Md Mustafa Hossain]. it has been held by Single Bench of this court that unlike an order of injunction which becomes operative upon being served on the party against whom it is directed. an order of stay takes effect immediately on being passed even if it is not brought to the notice of the subordinate Court. Thus, the very moment a stay order is passed proceedings of the suit could not be continued. It would since then remain in a state of suspended animation till disposal of the Rule. Mr Alam has also drawn our attention to two other decisions of the Indian Jurisdiction which have been referred to in the case of 47 CWN. Mr Alam submits that a Full Bench of Madras High Court in the case of Kasaribada vs Maddipatta (ILR 41 Mad 151) held that operation of stay order passed by an Appellate Court only commences from the time of its communication but a Full Bench of Allahabad High Court in the case of Passotam Saram vs Barlnanand (ILR 50 All 41) has taken a middle course and, according to that court, it operates from the time of its passing against parties to the proceedings but against strangers it operates from the time of its communication. Mr Mahbubey Alam then relies on an observation given in paragraph No. 10 by the Indian Supreme Court in the case of M/S Shree Chamundi Mopeds Ltd. vs Church of South India Trust Association, Madras. On the strength of the aforesaid decision Mr Mahbubey Alam submits that in the instant case admittedly the contemner respondents were informed for the first time bout the order of the court on 18-7-2001 whereas on 17-7-2001 they published the preliminary result of the election when they were not in the know of the injunction order and therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case by no stretch of imagination the contemner respondents could be held liable for violating the court's order on 17-7-2001. Mr Alam further submits that the news item published by the contemner respondents in the daily newspaper after obtaining the said stay order from the Appellate Division on 3rd of August. 2001 does not reflect the correct legal position and such publication has given rise to the present proceeding. The contemner respondents, therefore, pleaded for mercy if they had committed any contempt by making the press release for publication in the daily newspaper. 

 8. We would, therefore, like to enter into the merits of the case. The admitted position is that after the scrutiny of the nomination paper on 16th of July, 2001, 17th of July of 2001 was fixed for publishing valid list of candidates but on that date the preliminary result of the election was published by the Election Commissioner in view of the fact that there were no other candidates for the posts as there was only one panel of candidates for the posts. The preliminary result was declared on 17th July, 2001 although that was the date fixed for publishing of the final list of valid candidates. We have gone through the decisions relied on by Mr Alam. It appears that the observation of the Indian Supreme Court made in the case of M/S Shree Chamundi Mopeds Ltd has no manner of application to the present case inasmuch as the facts of the present case are quite distinguishable. We are of the opinion that we need not enter into the nicety of law as to when a stay order becomes operative since we are in seisin of a quasi-criminal matter where requirement of law is that the allegations must be proved to the hilt and a contemner is entitled to get the benefit of doubt. Keeping that principle in mind we would like to dispose of the matter on the basis of admitted facts. Therefore, we do not find fault with the contemner for publishing the preliminary result on 17-7-2001 on the ground that at that time they had no knowledge of the order dated 16-7-201 and admittedly it was communicated to them on 18-7-2001. 

 9. It may be mentioned that the contemner respondents having the knowledge of the order dated 16th of July, 2001 filed an application before this court on 26th of July, 2001 for vacating the order of stay but that application was rejected after hearing the parties. Thereafter, they filed a Civil Miscellaneous Petition before the Appellate Division on 30-7-2001 and obtained stay order in chamber operative till 14-8-2001 and while that stay order was in operation, the contemner respondent Nos. 2 and 3 published the final result of the election on 6-8-2001 and thereafter the newly elected members also held the first meeting on 9-8-2001. Now the only question that calls for determination is whether by the publication of the final result on 6-8-2001, the contemners have in any manner flouted or violated the court's order dated 16th of July, 2001. 

 10. The admitted position is that at that point of time the order of the High Court Division was not in force because of the stay order granted by the Appellate Division and taking advantage of that situation the contemner opposite parties published the final result on 6-8-2001 whereby the entire attempts of the writ petitioners have been frustrated and the Rule issued by this court in the aforesaid writ petition has been rendered infructuous. It is true that in the eye of law the injunction order dated 16-7-2001 was in a state of suspended animation due to stay order passed by the Appellate Division but fact remains that by taking advantage of that order the contemners published the final result of the election on 6-8-2001. No explanation whatsoever has been published by the contemners as to what prompted them to publish the result on 6th of August, 2001 whereas stay order was obtained from the Appellate Division on 30-7-2001. The legal position is that the Election Commissioner is not a party to the election; they are entrusted with the job of preparing the voters list and holding the election. We do not find any reasons what actuated the contemner opposite parties to publish the final result on 6th August. 2001 when the stay order was going to expire on 14th of August, 2001. It further appears from the order dated 23rd of August, 2001 that their Lordships of the Appellate Division also observed that by taking advantage of the stay the respondents (present contemners) have published the final result of the election and thereby committed the mischief. 

 "Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides it appears that as yet the respondents in writ petition have not filed any affidavit but simply moved the High Court Division for getting the order of stay vacated and when they failed they approached this Division in the chamber and got an order of stay. But taking advantage of this order of stay the respondents in the writ petition under the signature of the General Secretary, Mosharraf Hossain Khan called a meeting of the Federation to be held on 9-8-2001 for introducing new committee of the federation. This indicates that the respondents of the writ petition got the result of the election published taking advantage of the order of stay from this Division and committed mischief. This has been done without filing any affidavit-in-opposition before the High Court Division and taking advantage of this order of stay at the instance of the general secretary of the Federation some steps have been taken which tantamount to mischief which cannot be allowed to be done and we are inclined to vacate our order of stay and accordingly, the order of stay passed by this Division in the Chamber is hereby vacated". 

 Therefore, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that although the order dated 16th of July, 2001 was stayed by the Appellate Division but oy finally publishing the result of the election on 6-8-2001 the contemners have committed contempt of this court. 

 It is not just and proper on the part of the Government servants who are entrusted with the sacred duty of holding the election of the Federation to act in such a manner to set at naught the court proceedings. It appears that ultimately, the contemner Nos. 2 & 3 sailed in the same boat with contemner No. 1 and being influenced by him published the final result on 6-8-2001. We have already indicated that the contemner Nos. 2 and 3 could not assign any reason why they have published the final result on 6-8-2001 and they have done so with the ill motive of helping the so-called newly elected members. By the said act they have definitely flouted the authority of this court and also obstructed the course of justice. The view taken by us gets support from the case reported in 15 DLR (SC) 355 [AG, West Pakistan vs Shabir Ahmed} wherein it has been held that any attempt to pollute the stream of justice before it has begun to flow or to interfere with its proper and unfettered administration will amount to a contempt. Further, in the case reported in 1990 BLD 73 = 41 DLR 508 [Thera Nargis vs Shamsur Rahman] it has been held that in contempt matter the intention of the contemner is not relevant. It is the effect of the contemner's action which is to be taken into consideration in deciding whether a contempt is committed or not. In the instant case the effect of the contemner's action is that they have deprived this court of its opportunity to adjudicate upon a matter which is knowingly pending before this court. By declaring final result, the dignity and authority of this court have been trampled and transgressed before the very eyes of the petitioners. This court cannot be a silent spectator to this state of affairs. Therefore, we find contemner Nos. 2 and 3 guilty of contempt of this court for publishing the final result of the election on 6-8-2001. 

 12. We find substance and force in this submission. Within the four comers of the record we do not find anything which shows that the respondent No.1 has any hand in getting the result published on 6-8-2001. Therefore, it appears that the allegation levelled against contemner respondent No. 1 falls to the ground. Therefore, we find him not guilty.
